title: Decode Ways II
summary: Given a string s consisting of digits and '*', return the number of ways to decode it, modulo 10^9 + 7 .
statement: Given a string s consisting of digits and '*', return the number of ways to decode it, modulo 10^9 + 7 . The '*' character can represent any digit from '1' to '9'. For example, '1*' can represent '11', '12', ..., '19'. Digits 'A' to 'Z' are mapped to '1' to '26'. The mapping rules for decoding must be followed, and the grouping of digits must be valid according to the given constraints.
constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 100,000; s contains digits and * only.
* represents a digit from 1 through 9; return the decoding count modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Each position contributes through one-character and two-character decodings with wildcard multiplicities.
Roll a two-state dynamic program and multiply by the number of valid substitutions.
current = singleWays*dp[i-1] + pairWays*dp[i-2], modulo the limit.
The final token of every decoding has length one or two, producing disjoint cases counted by the recurrence.
editorial: The final token of every decoding has length one or two, producing disjoint cases counted by the recurrence.
